subject: Recap: suitability snapshot & performance appendix for ClearPath pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Bowen <claire.bowen@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: suitability snapshot & performance appendix for ClearPath pilot

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap + recommended next steps so we have a single source of truth after the discussion.

Key call takeaways
- Primary goal: excerpt generation and short-form summarization for clinical notes (avg input ~420 tokens, expected output ~120 tokens).
- Latency/p99 target: <= 350 ms for 512 token inference; cost sensitivity: prioritized but willing to trade up to ~20% higher cost for consistent quality.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC peering required for pilot.

Immediate recommendations (model + small pilot)
1) Model shortlist (recommended order)
   - Redwood-13B-opt (quantized int8): best cost/latency balance for your throughput profile (80–120 TPS on a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with batching heuristics).
   - Llama2-70B-8k (fp16): higher single-request quality for tricky medical terminologies — expect ~3x the latency and 2–3x cost vs Redwood-13B-opt.
   - OpenMed-15B-tuned (fp16 + optimized kernels): good middle ground for specialty terms; variability observed on long prefixes.

2) Benchmarks & artifacts I’m sharing
   - Redwood-verified performance appendix (p50/p90/p99) for the three models at seq len 256/512: see attachment clearpath_benchmarks_v2.pdf and hosted report link below.
   - Prompt set v3 (zip) with representative clinical prompts we used for quality checks: prompt-sets-v3.zip.
   - Lightweight pilot SOW draft: sow_smallpilot_v1.docx (scope + acceptance criteria).

3) Quality regression guards
- We recommend a guarded rollout: small canary (1% traffic) -> model shadowing -> progressive ramp with automated evals on your prompt set (we provide the evaluation harness).
- Suggested regression thresholds: BLEU/ROUGE/Exact-match delta tolerance = -2% relative to baseline; human review sampling 1% of outputs for first two weeks.

Next steps (concrete)
- I’ll share the benchmark links and artifacts now. Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync next week (Priyom + Kimberly + your eng lead) to agree pilot metrics and access (VPC peering + service accounts)?
- If you’re happy, we’ll provision a small Dedicated pool for a 2-week pilot and run the Redwood-13B-opt profile first.

Attachments:
- clearpath_benchmarks_v2.pdf (performance appendix)
- prompt-sets-v3.zip (input prompts + expected outputs)
- sow_smallpilot_v1.docx (pilot SOW)

Links:
- Hosted perf report: https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/benchmarks/clearpath_v2/index.html
- Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExAMPLEclearpath

Subject: Re: Recap: suitability snapshot & performance appendix for ClearPath pilot

Hi Claire — good question. Short answer: the numbers I referenced are model-side (server) latencies measured with our Redwood runtime and include kernel execution + queuing but exclude last-mile network egress from your VPC. For planning, you should budget ~30–70 ms network overhead depending on your region and peering.

Redwood-13B-opt (quantized int8) — verified snapshot @ seq_len=512 (server-side):
- p50: 42 ms
- p90: 96 ms
- p99: 290 ms
- sustained TPS (observed, 4 x A40-like GPUs with continuous batching): ~95 TPS for 512-token inference; peak burst ~120 TPS with smart routing enabled.

For comparison:
- Llama2-70B-8k (fp16): p99 ~820 ms, sustained TPS ~30
- OpenMed-15B-tuned: p99 ~410 ms, sustained TPS ~45

What I’m attaching is the raw perf appendix and the per-profile heatmaps (clearpath_benchmarks_v2.pdf). The hosted report also has interactive slices by sequence-length distribution and batching window.

Quality notes
- On our representative prompt set (prompt-sets-v3), Redwood-13B-opt hits parity for extraction tasks and slightly underperforms the 70B variant in edge cases (rare medical terms). We recommend running the pilot on Redwood-13B-opt with a fixed fallback policy to 70B for queries flagged as low-confidence (we can instrument that).

If that looks good, can we lock in 60 minutes for the technical sync next Tuesday (US PST)? I’ll have Priyom join to scope instrumentation and the canary rollout.

Ben

Attachments referenced: clearpath_benchmarks_v2.pdf, prompt-sets-v3.zip
